facts.statement: The holotype of Kaiwhekea was discovered in 1983 by amateur fossil collector Gary Raper at Shag Point, Otago.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in 1983 by Gary Raper, an amateur fossil collector, at the base of a cliff at Shag Point, Otago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found inside a concretion weighing an estimated 10 tons.
facts.quote: The specimen was enclosed in a large concretion measuring metres long and weighing an estimated 10 tons.

facts.statement: The skeleton is preserved mostly as negative moulds because the original mineralized bone was too fragile to survive.
facts.quote: The skeleton is mostly preserved as negative moulds as the mineralised bone was too fragile to be preserved.

facts.statement: The genus name Kaiwhekea translates to "squid-eater" from Māori words meaning "food" and "squid".
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the Māori words kai meaning "food" and whekea meaning "squid", together meaning "squid-eater".

facts.statement: Kaiwhekea was approximately 6.5 to 7 meters long.
Kaiwhekea lived around 70 to 69 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived around 70-69 million years ago.

facts.statement: Kaiwhekea is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) of what is now New Zealand.
facts.quote: Kaiwhekea () is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) of what is now New Zealand.

facts.statement: Kaiwhekea has been classified as an aristonectine plesiosaur closely related to Aristonectes.
facts.quote: Kaiwhekea has been placed as an aristonectine plesiosaur close to Aristonectes.

facts.statement: In 2010, Kaiwhekea was transferred to the family Leptocleididae, but recent analyses do not support this placement.
facts.quote: In 2010, Kaiwhekea was transferred to Leptocleididae, but more recent analyses do not find the same result.

facts.statement: Kaiwhekea has been classified as an aristonectine plesiosaur close to Aristonectes (O'Keefe and Street, 2009).
facts.quote: Kaiwhekea ha sido clasificado como un plesiosaurio aristonéctido cercano a Aristonectes (O'Keefe y Street, 2009).

facts.statement: In 2010, Kaiwhekea was transferred to the family Leptocleididae.
facts.quote: En 2010, Kaiwhekea fue transferido a la familia Leptocleididae.

facts.statement: Kaiwhekea belongs to the parent group Weddellonectia.
Kaiwhekea is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
The time range for Kaiwhekea spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The type species, Kaiwhekea katiki, was first described by Arthur Cruickshank and Ewan Fordyce in 2002.
